object_context: Source-bound quantitative repair child of YM-E2a (#73): at fixed physical transfer time tau, determine whether the Faizal–Shabir RG defect estimates actually prove a positive margin delta0 - sum_k epsilon_k > 0 uniformly in volume, rather than only summability.
structural_coordinates: fixed-physical-time transfer gap Delta_{k,L}=1-||T_{k,L}|Q|| versus Hamiltonian gap -tau^{-1}log(1-Delta)
initial strong-coupling lower bound delta0 and its parameter/volume dependence
defect sequence epsilon_k and exact operator-norm definition
Proposition 5.5 constants C, theta and their block-factor/FRD/collar dependence
total budget sum epsilon_k versus delta0, not summability alone
volume uniformity and same RG trajectory
first-defect versus tail dependence when block factor is enlarged
equivalent_formulations: positive margin: inf_k,L Delta_{k,L} >= delta0-sum epsilon_k > 0
geometric sufficient condition: if epsilon_k <= C theta^k then C/(1-theta) < delta0
first-term/tail split: epsilon_0 + sum_{k>=1} epsilon_k < delta0
Hamiltonian fixed-tau form: m0 - tau^{-1} sum epsilon_k > 0
solved_analogues: Abstract telescoping stability: x_{k+1}>=x_k-e_k implies x_n>=x_0-sum_{j<n}e_j; positivity needs total loss strictly below the initial reserve.
near_solved_analogues: Faizal–Shabir Proposition 5.5 supplies a summable geometric envelope epsilon_k<=C theta^k but issue #73 records that the source-facing positive-margin constant chain remains unbound.

method_transfers.repair_question: Does the actual source prove a parameter choice for which the full same-theory loss budget is strictly below the strong-coupling reserve?

explicit_disanalogies: A generic geometric-series estimate does not determine the source constants C or theta.
Making a tail decay faster cannot by itself control epsilon_0 if its prefactor or first-scale geometry does not shrink.
The main-text variable-a_k gap route is a separate normalization problem (#92); this atom stays at fixed tau.
A source-local repair would not by itself establish continuum OS identification, source completeness, or asymptotic freedom.
